title: Iraq’s Oil Minister Denies Ouster Rumors as Najaf Smuggling Scandal Widens
content:
Iraq’s Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair al-Abadi on Monday denied media reports  that prime minister Ali Al Zaidi was considering dismissing him following the discovery of possible oil smuggling operations in the Iraqi province of Najaf this weekend. 

"The issue of resignation is completely unfounded," al-Abadi said in a statement, adding that he fully supports the government’s anti-corruption efforts.

Al-Abadi’s reaction came after Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council on Saturday said a court issued arrest warrants against the head of the Energy Committee at the Najaf Provincial Council and his brother after an investigating judge conducted a field inspection in a plot of land belonging to the siblings.

The judge found “encroachment on one of the oil pipelines in the Najaf Governorate,” the statement said, adding that the two men “had previously dug a trench surrounding the plot of land on all sides, hindering access and preventing people from observing the activities taking place there.”

title: U.K. Seizes $72 Million Tied to Singapore Scandal, Drawing Scrutiny Over Early Deals
content:
Britain’s National Crime Agency has seized more than $70 million in properties tied to Singapore’s $2.3 billion money-laundering scandal, an outcome which, although hailed as a success in combating financial crime, has been criticized by an expert as a “missed opportunity” for the larger recoveries and greater accountability that a trial would likely have brought.

The NCA named last week Su Haijin and Xu Haika as two individuals “linked to an international money laundering network that had agreed to hand over around £55 million ($72.1 million) in assets after being pursued by the NCA”, in a settlement that was approved by the U.K. High Court.

OCCRP has reported extensively on the U.K. and global asset portfolio of both men, including Su Haijin’s purchase of a townhouse on Oxford Street, and Xu Haika’s purchases of multiple luxury apartments further down the same bustling high street. 

“These settlements are in the public interest, avoiding protracted and costly High Court litigation while enabling our resources to be redirected towards new investigations," said Gareth Jones, Branch Commander for Asset Denial at the National Crime Agency.

title: US Sanctions Italian Mafia Group in Canada and Australian Biker Gang with Global Footprint
content:
The latest U.S. sanctions against organized crime stretch from Canada, home to a powerful faction of an Italian mafia group, to Australia where an outlaw motorcycle gang grew into an international drug dealing organization.

Both the Comancheros motorcycle gang and the Toronto-based ‘Ndrangheta mafia faction have ties to Mexican cocaine cartels, according to a statement on Thursday by the U.S. Treasury Department. 

“The Comancheros and the ‘Ndrangheta operate sophisticated transnational criminal networks that facilitate large-scale drug trafficking and money laundering,” the Treasury said.

Three of the sanctioned alleged ‘Ndrangheta members were featured in a multi-part investigation into the Canadian faction published in 2024 by OCCRP, the Toronto Star, and La Repubblica.

One article revealed that Angelo Figliomeni, the group’s alleged boss, was in contact with Toronto-area real estate developers, and was linked to a sprawling property empire.

title: Wine Distributor Targeted in Latest US Prince Group Sanctions Owns Warehouse Unit in London
content:
A man sanctioned this month for his alleged role in the Prince Group — a Cambodian conglomerate accused by the U.S. of operating major cyber-scams — controls a warehouse unit in London through his now-sanctioned wine distribution company, property documents show.

The U.S. Treasury Department imposed its third round of sanctions on the Prince Group on November 5, designating it as a “Transnational Criminal Organization (TCO)” and alleging it was involved in “cyber-enabled fraud, money laundering, and human trafficking.”

A Prince Group spokesperson told OCCRP the Treasury Department has “no support for any of their latest allegations,” adding: “Once again, the U.S. Government has issued new sanctions with zero factual basis for their claims.”

Included among the newly-sanctioned entities and individuals was Chinese-born Qiu Yong, 39, who holds citizenships from Cambodia, Saint Lucia and Turkey, according to the Treasury Department.

title: Accused South American Drug Lord Faces US Trial after Judge Rejects Motions
content:
Sebastián Marset, an accused South American drug lord, appears headed for a January jury trial after a federal judge in Virginia this week rejected multiple efforts by the defense to dismiss charges.

U.S. District Judge Rossie Alston Jr. on Tuesday rejected arguments from Marset’s lawyers that the Uruguayan national was being subjected to a vindictive prosecution and misconduct by prosecutors.

Marset’s defense team had argued their client’s Miranda rights, which protect against self-incrimination, were violated when agents from the Drug Enforcement Administration interviewed him without a lawyer present.

But the judge held that Marset had initiated some of the conversations after his arrest in southern Bolivia and was not coerced into talking with DEA agents during his expulsion to Peru and subsequent transfer to the United States and custody in Virginia.

The judge also rejected the defense’s “fruit of the poisonous tree” motion that asserted that evidence should be excluded because it was obtained improperly.
snippet: Sebastián Marset, an accused South American drug lord, appears headed for a January jury trial after a federal judge in Virginia this week rejected multiple efforts by the defense to dismiss charges.

title: British Hacker Admits Breaching Uber, Revolut and Rockstar
content:
A member of the notorious Lapsus$ cybercrime group pleaded guilty on Monday to hacking several major international companies, including Uber, Revolut and Rockstar Games, the developer of the Grand Theft Auto video game franchise.

Arion Kurtaj, 21, formerly of Oxfordshire, admitted six offenses at Woolwich Crown Court in London, including computer misuse, fraud and possessing an unauthorized mobile phone in prison. He is due to be sentenced on November 23.

Prosecutors said Kurtaj was involved in a series of cyberattacks between 2021 and 2022 that compromised customer and employee information, disrupted corporate systems and resulted in the theft and publication of commercially sensitive material.

“Arion Kurtaj used sophisticated hacking techniques to carry out a sustained campaign of cyberattacks, causing serious disruption to major international business and putting sensitive information at risk,” said Robert Hutchinson, a specialist prosecutor with the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS).

title: Kyrgyz Man Sentenced to Three Years For Re-Posting Video on Facebook
content:
A Kyrgyzstan court has sentenced a construction worker and father of four children to three years in penal colony for a Facebook post that was critical of authorities. 

Baktybek Moldaliev, 48, was sentenced last week in the capital, Bishkek, on charges of “distribution of extremist materials.” The material in question is a video by the investigative media outlet Kloop, which he re-posted along with a comment.

While Moldaliev was convicted over the post he made in April, court files obtained by OCCRP show that Kyrgyz authorities had been collecting evidence against him for at least six months before that. 

Police searched Moldaliev’s apartment in November 2025, and brought him to the Ministry of Internal Affairs for questioning about his social media activity. The files do not show any charge against him at that time.

The Ministry of Internal Affairs did not respond to a request for comment.

Moldaliev was detained and questioned again on May 8, according to the files.

He told police: “I had been writing posts expressing my personal opinions on political and social issues occurring in the Kyrgyz Republic, specifically regarding the high cost of living, unemployment, and corruption.”

title: Iraq Cracks Down on Oil Smuggling in Area Controlled by Iran-aligned Shiite Militias
content:
In a rare bid to assert state authority inside a paramilitary-controlled enclave, the Iraqi government has launched a campaign to dismantle oil smuggling networks in Jurf al-Nasr, a stronghold of Iran-backed militias along the Euphrates River, roughly 30 miles southwest of the capital.

The crackdown takes direct aim at an illicit fuel trade operating inside an area that has long functioned outside of Baghdad’s authority.

The move followed the leak of an intelligence report, seen by OCCRP, that detailed the smuggling operation and included satellite imagery showing container truck movements between pipelines and local storage facilities from 2022 to 2026. The report cited evidence of perforated oil pipelines and makeshift storage facilities, adding that the armed groups controlling the area smuggled the fuel along three suspected routes leading into Baghdad province.

title: Switzerland is Prosecuting the First Journalist Under its Banking Secrecy Law. The EU Has No Comment.
content:
The unprecedented criminal prosecution of a journalist under Switzerland's stringent banking secrecy law is raising alarms among press freedom advocates across Europe. But the European Union has nothing to say about it.

Lukas Hässig, founder of the financial news website Inside Paradeplatz, was charged in October over articles published a decade ago. The articles cited leaked information, and focused on financial dealings involving former Raiffeisen Switzerland chief executive Pierin Vincenz, and his business partner Beat Stocker.

The revelations helped trigger investigations that eventually led to criminal proceedings. In April 2022, Vincenz and Stocker were convicted of fraud and other offenses. Vincenz was sentenced to three years and nine months in prison, while Stocker received a four-year term. Both have appealed, with a ruling expected in January 2027.

Separately, Stocker filed a criminal complaint asking prosecutors to pursue charges against Hässig.

"There is a public interest in the facts. An unsubstantiated, flawed narrative is another matter," Stocker told OCCRP, arguing that there was “no legal basis under Swiss criminal law” for his own conviction.

title: Buro Media Launches Database of Lukashenko’s Inner Circle
content:
OCCRP’s Belarusian member center Buro Media has launched Friday a new database, “Favorites,” documenting the wealth, assets, business interests, and connections of people close to Belarusian authoritarian leader Aleksandr Lukashenko.

The project currently features 20 profiles, including members of Lukashenko’s family, security officials, businessmen, and public figures. Buro plans to expand the database with additional names.

Each profile provides biographical information, details of business activities, and current and historical assets held by the individuals and their associates. The database also documents personal and professional connections, sanctions, criminal proceedings, and privileges granted through ties to Lukashenko, including preferential government loans, tax exemptions, state contracts, and exclusive import and export rights.

title: US Prosecutors Ask Judge to Allow Bribery Evidence in South American Drug Trafficking Case
content:
American prosecutors want to introduce examples of encrypted communications and alleged bribery of government officials as part of their case against accused South American drug baron Sebastián Marset.

In pretrial motions filed this week, the Justice Department argued the evidence is necessary to give jurors a full picture of Marset’s alleged global drug trafficking network ahead of a trial expected early next year.  

Prosecutors told District Judge Rossie Alston Jr. that the evidence will also show Marset engaged in a conspiracy to launder drug proceeds.

Marset was arrested in a pre-dawn raid in Santa Cruz, Bolivia, in March and expelled to the U.S. with the assistance of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration. He was initially charged with money laundering counts, but was later indicted on drug trafficking and narco-terrorism charges.

Marset’s lawyers argue that the initial charge of money laundering is invalid because it involved a single wire transfer between Portugal and China that did not involve the servers of a U.S. bank. They say Marset never trafficked drugs to the U.S., and the narco-terrorism groups were not designated as such at the time of his dealing with them.

title: Kazakh Wealth Fund, Railway Chiefs Detained in Corruption Probe
content:
Kazakhstan’s anti-corruption service on Wednesday detained the heads of the country’s sovereign wealth fund and national railway operator on suspicion of a corruption offense.

The detained officials are Nurlan Zhakupov, head of the Samruk-Kazyna Sovereign Fund—which holds about $87.5 billion in assets—and Yelzhas Otynshiyev, head of the national railway company Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ), the country’s National Security Committee said in a statement Thursday. KTZ is a subsidiary of the fund and operates the country’s main rail network.

Alongside other officials, whom the committee did not name, Zhakupov and Otynshiyev are “suspected of committing a corruption-related offense,” the committee said, adding that “investigative actions are currently underway to establish all the circumstances of the case.” 

Footage published on the X account of the national broadcaster Qazaqstan, showed Zhakupov, wearing a blue shirt, surrounded by several people in a doorway.

A representative of Samruk-Kazyna, told the local media outlet Tengrinews that the fund is fully cooperating with law enforcement.
snippet: Kazakhstan’s anti-corruption service on Wednesday detained the heads of the country’s sovereign wealth fund and national railway operator on suspicion of a corruption offense.

title: More Than 1,300 Diplomatic Passports Missing in Vanuatu, Report Finds
content:
A damning parliamentary report in Vanuatu has found more than 1,300 diplomatic passports went missing in recent years and remain unaccounted for.

The report by Vanuatu’s Public Accounts Committee, released on Tuesday and obtained by OCCRP, revealed that 1,390 diplomatic passports went missing between 2019 and 2024, with 1,301 disappearing in 2024 alone.

The committee also found significant irregularities in the processing and issuance of the documents, including alleged misuse by the country’s prime minister and foreign minister.

It is the latest passport controversy for the small Pacific island country of roughly 340,000 people, whose so-called “golden passport” program has attracted a colorful cast of wealthy investors ranging from spies and fugitives to sanctioned oligarchs and influencer Andrew Tate.

The report followed several years of mounting concerns over the country’s issuance of diplomatic passports.

title: UK Arrests 349 in Nationwide Money Laundering Crackdown
content:
The UK's National Crime Agency (NCA) announced that 349 people had been arrested in a nationwide crackdown on businesses suspected of laundering criminal proceeds. During October, police inspected or raided 3,029 premises, including barbershops, vape stores and other cash-intensive businesses, seizing approximately $2.9 million in cash and obtaining court orders to freeze another $4.9 million in bank accounts. Authorities also identified or prevented an estimated $5.5 million in tax evasion and seized illicit goods worth nearly $9 million.

The operation was the latest phase of Operation Machinize, a nationwide campaign targeting businesses used to conceal criminal profits. An earlier phase of the crackdown resulted in more than 900 arrests and inspections of over 2,700 businesses. The NCA estimates that at least $1.3 billion in criminal proceeds is laundered through such businesses in the UK annually. The agency said the campaign is increasingly focused on identifying the criminal networks behind the businesses rather than just individual premises.

title: Bosnian Raids Smash Two Crime Rings, Net 15 Arrests
content:
Bosnian authorities arrested 15 people in a sweeping multi-agency operation aimed at dismantling two organized crime groups suspected of drug trafficking and money laundering, the Zenica-Doboj Canton Ministry of Interior announced Wednesday. Thirteen suspects were detained in the Zenica-Doboj Canton and two in Sarajevo with all scheduled to be transferred to the Federal Police Administration for further questioning.

The raids resulted in the seizure of more than 100,000 convertible marks ($56,735) in cash, nine cars, a motorcycle, weapons, and drug-weighing equipment, according to the statement. The ministry noted that ongoing law enforcement activities related to the case have so far led to the seizure of about 150 kilograms of narcotics and 83 liters of oil used for amphetamine production.

The Federal Prosecutor's Office, which supervised the crackdown alongside the Supreme Court, stated that the broader operational activities targeted "dozens of individuals" to gather evidence documenting the syndicates' crimes. Searches were executed across four cantons, as well as in Republika Srpska, in coordination with the state intelligence agency and federal police.

title: Kyrgyz Government Sold Mountain Resort to NGO Tied to Sanctioned Russian Influence Effort
content:
For years, the Bars resort, perched in the foothills above Kyrgyzstan’s iconic Issyk-Kul lake, attracted local and foreign visitors with its picturesque views and athletic facilities.

Few of them would have known that the resort, named after the mountainous Central Asian nation’s famous snow leopards, belonged to the family of the country’s most notorious criminal boss. 

Kamchi Kolbayev, the alleged head of a network involved in drug, arms, and human trafficking, extortion, and other crimes, was killed in a special operation by the Kyrgyz state security service (GKNB) in 2023. The agency subsequently released a video listing his seized assets, including the Bars complex.

In public remarks last month, Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov said his government had sold off the resort for $12 million, or double its value, to a local businessman. “That money went to the state budget,” Japarov said.

But an investigation by OCCRP has found that the government received no such windfall — the GKNB had originally valued the resort at $20 million — and that its actual buyer in 2025 was an obscure NGO with no website or public activity called Edinstvo Naroda (“Unity of the People”).

title: Interpol Crackdown on Migrant Smuggling Nets 262 Arrests
content:
An Interpol-led operation across 16 countries has resulted in 262 arrests tied to migrant smuggling networks along the Mediterranean Sea and West African Atlantic routes, the agency announced Tuesday. The four-day sweep across North and West Africa, southern Europe, and the Middle East identified 109 potential human trafficking victims, detected 1,715 irregular migrants, and sparked 434 new investigations that are “expected to yield further leads and arrests in the coming weeks and months.”

Among the key interventions, Moroccan authorities rescued a vessel carrying 70 stranded migrants—including 30 minors—who had been at sea for six days. In a separate action, Mauritanian law enforcement intercepted a wooden boat carrying 80 passengers and arrested three suspected organizers.

title: Ex-Belgrade Police Chief Denies Charges in 'Body in a Barrel' Case
content:
A former Belgrade police chief pleaded not guilty to charges stemming from a brazen gangland murder, while prosecutors have dropped the most severe allegations against him.

Former Police Chief Veselin Milić appeared Monday before the First Basic Court in Belgrade to deny charges of failing to report a crime and falsifying an official document, OCCRP’s Serbian member center KRIK reported.

In addition to those charges prosecutors had previously accused him of participating in covering up the physical traces of the May 12 murder of Aleksandar Nešović, whose body was discovered stuffed in a barrel that had been buried in the town of Inđija after a week-long search. Prosecutors have now withdrawn those allegations, while the investigator who built the case has been arrested on suspicion of illegally gathering evidence against Milić.

Milić was removed from his post as Belgrade's police chief, but he currently serves as an Assistant Director of Police.
snippet: A former Belgrade police chief pleaded not guilty to charges stemming from a brazen gangland murder, while prosecutors have dropped the most severe allegations against him.

title: High-Profile Smuggling Raids in Hungary Point to Former PM's Brother
content:
Hungarian authorities arrested multiple suspects in coordinated human smuggling raids on Monday morning, an operation that local media and political figures say resulted in the detention of Áron Orbán, the younger brother of former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.

The National Bureau of Investigation (NNI) and the National Asset Recovery and Asset Protection Office (NVVH) conducted simultaneous house searches across Budapest and Pest County. While police confirmed the multi-agency operation in a public statement, they did not immediately release the identities of those detained.

News outlet Kontroll.hu reported that the former premier's brother may have been among those arrested in connection with an NVVH probe into a visa facilitation network.

The reports prompted a public exchange between the former premier and current Prime Minister Péter Magyar.

Viktor Orbán indirectly confirmed his brother's arrest in a Facebook post, condemning the police action as a politically motivated "settling of scores" designed to distract from an "agent scandal" facing the current government.

title: Paraguayan President Impeached and Arrested Amid Financial Meltdown and Mass Protests
content:
Paraguayan President Santiago Peña has been impeached and arrested amid a financial crisis that triggered mass protests, and turned his own Colorado party against him.

The crisis was sparked by a major digital bank being ordered into insolvency earlier in the week. Peña previously had shares in the holding company that owned the digital lender, Ueno Bank. Peña has denied allegations that he helped protect Ueno from scrutiny.

In addition to holding public funds, Ueno banked millions of private citizens who have now been left without access to their accounts. 

In a Thursday statement announcing his resignation, posted to Facebook, Peña said his “greatest wish” was that funds would be returned to Ueno customers. He said he was resigning in order to "bring calm to the population."

By that time, the streets of downtown Asunción, the nation's capital, were teeming with protesters. In the Chamber of Deputies, both his allies and opponents rejected Peña’s resignation, and instead proceeded with an impeachment process. 

The matter then fell to senators who held an extraordinary session on Friday. Peña did not appear in person for his defense in the Senate, though he sent his lawyer, Ricardo Preda.
snippet: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña has been impeached and arrested amid a financial crisis that triggered mass protests, and turned his own Colorado party against him.

title: Cyber Incident Disrupts French Blood Storage Systems
content:
The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said a cybersecurity incident involving one of its refrigeration equipment providers disrupted cold storage systems at three of its sites, causing temperature and defrost settings to rise to unusually high levels.

The incident occurred on November 2, according to a statement published by EFS the following day. The organization said it was not directly targeted, but the attack on its provider affected systems used to monitor and control refrigeration units.

EFS said its alarm systems enabled staff to respond promptly, ensuring that no blood samples or products were compromised. As a precaution, the contents of the affected refrigeration units were transferred to other facilities.

The statement confirmed information reported earlier by the French satirical newspaper Le Canard enchaîné, which identified refrigeration equipment provider Coolworld as the apparent target of the incident.

Coolworld also acknowledged a cybersecurity incident involving remote monitoring software used in refrigeration systems, although it did not explicitly link the incident to EFS.

title: Ukraine Uncovers Crime Ring Allegedly Shielded by Officials
content: Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) and Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAP) uncovered an alleged criminal organization involving at least 12 people, including serving senior officials from Ukraine's Security Service (SBU), the Prosecutor General's Office and the National Police. NABU and SAP announced Thursday that five alleged members had been formally notified of suspicion, including senior SBU and police officials whose names were not disclosed. Investigators said the group provided protection to fraudulent call centers targeting Ukrainians and foreigners, as well as operations involving illegal drug sales and the production of counterfeit cigarettes and foreign currency. The organization allegedly used corrupt connections within law enforcement to shield its activities and was involved in planned attacks, kidnappings and assaults.

title: Hackers Steal Estimated 118 Million Euros in Cyberattack on French Bank
content:
French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa suffered a sophisticated cyberattack that allegedly siphoned an estimated 118 million euros ($132.44 million) from its corporate accounts, though the institution stated that client assets were untouched.

In a Wednesday public statement and a subsequent update, the bank explained that hackers infiltrated its systems through a third-party service provider's platform. The attackers bypassed client accounts entirely, using Crédit Mutuel Arkéa’s proprietary accounts to transfer funds to other banks. The stolen money was then potentially converted into cryptocurrency on specialized platforms, the bank said.

Addressing media reports that 118 million euros were stolen, the bank did not confirm the exact figure but validated the "order of magnitude."

title: Iraq Jails Ex-Oil Boss for Eight Years Over $119M Kickback Scheme
content:
A high-profile court ruling against a senior former oil official has delivered another warning to Iraq’s political establishment that high office no longer guarantees impunity, an influential lawmaker told OCCRP on Wednesday, as authorities widen an aggressive anti-corruption campaign across the country’s lucrative energy sector.

The verdict sends “a clear message that positions and responsibilities do not grant immunity from accountability,” said Qaisar al-Jorani, a member of parliament’s committee on oil, gas, and natural resources, calling the misappropriation of state wealth a “red line that must not be crossed.”

The ruling, handed down by Iraq’s Criminal Court for Combating Corruption, sentenced Hussein Talib Abboud, the former director general of the State Company for Oil Products Distribution, to eight years in prison and ordered him to repay 55 billion Iraqi dinars (nearly $36.2 million).

title: US Sentences Venezuelan National to 12 Years for Laundering Over $1 Billion
content:
A U.S. district court sentenced a 60-year-old Venezuelan national Jorge Figueira to 12 years in prison and ordered him to surrender $1 billion for running a money laundering network tied to drug trafficking organizations, according to a Tuesday statement.

Investigators found that Figueira's operation moved over $1 billion through a single cryptocurrency wallet and various financial accounts. The network funneled the illicit funds into and out of the U.S. using shell companies, traditional bank accounts, and cryptocurrency exchanges, directing outbound money to individuals and businesses worldwide, including in Colombia, China, Panama, and Mexico.

title: Donald Trump Jr. Discussed Deals With Russian Businessman Close to Putin’s Personal Security Chief, Two Sources Say
content:
Donald Trump Jr. makes no secret of his relationship with Kremlin-linked businessman Umar Kremlev.

In 2025, the two men appeared together on stage in Istanbul at a meeting of the International Boxing Association, of which Kremlev is president. “I am proud to call Umar not only a leader but a friend,” Trump Jr. said.

And earlier this year, after ProPublica revealed that Kremlev had rented out a private island for Trump Jr.’s wedding, his new wife posted on Instagram that this had been “an extraordinarily generous” gift from “our dear friend Umar.”

But now, as reported by OCCRP’s Russian partner Important Stories, there may be more than friendship on the agenda. Two sources independently told the outlet’s reporters that Kremlev told them he and Trump Jr. had met in Kazakhstan to discuss business deals earlier this year.

Kremlev referred to those encounters as “business meetings,” they said. Both sources were quoted anonymously to ensure their safety.
snippet: Donald Trump Jr. makes no secret of his relationship with Kremlin-linked businessman Umar Kremlev.

title: Nepal Anti-Graft Body Charges Ex-PM Madhav Nepal, 96 Others With Corruption
content:
Nepal’s anti-corruption agency on Tuesday filed corruption charges against former Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal and 96 others over an alleged land-swap scheme that investigators say cost the government roughly $4.8 million.

The case, brought by the Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA), centers on the illegal sale of land that should have been returned to government ownership, according to a commission statement.

The CIAA also charged Minendra Prasad Rijal who served as minister for federal affairs and parliamentary affairs and coordinator of the cabinet’s social committee at the time of the alleged scheme.

“Summons will be issued for all of them starting tomorrow to appear in court,” Parwati Hitan, the Special Court’s information officer, told OCCRP. She said defendants will have 15 days to appear, and that this can be extended by seven days. None has been detained.

“Once they appear, their statements will be recorded, and after their statements, the hearing process moves forward,” Hitan said. Witness statements and evidence would follow before a bench issues a final decision, she added.

title: DRC Orders Probe into Illegal Mining Following Major Copper and Cobalt Seizure
content:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo will open an investigation into suspected mining fraud and widespread illegal mining, following the seizure of thousands of tons of copper and cobalt as well as more than 500 trucks and other machines, according to a statement by the Justice Ministry.

The probe comes two weeks after Congo's mines minister suspended the head of the state agency overseeing artisanal and ​small-scale mining, accusing him of failing to prevent illegal ‌mining on licensed concessions.

As the world’s largest producer of cobalt and second-largest producer of copper, the Democratic Republic of the Congo has long struggled with unauthorized miners and cross-border smuggling rings encroaching on industrial concessions held by foreign operators.

title: Serbian Bank Tied to Outgoing Regime Collapses After Internal Vault Theft
content:
A Serbian commercial court officially launched bankruptcy proceedings against Belgrade-based Alta Banka on Tuesday and activated a state mechanism to refund depositors, just one day after top executives were arrested for allegedly stealing more than 45.5 billion Serbian dinars (more than $427 million) from the institution's vault.

The financial collapse stems from a massive alleged internal theft. In coordinated statements on Monday, the Public Prosecutor's Office for Organized Crime and the Interior Ministry confirmed the detention of the "responsible person" of Alta Banka, identified by authorities only by the initials D.M. (born 1981). The Serbian branch of regional N1 TV subsequently identified the suspect as Davor Macura. Also arrested were the director of the treasury and cash management department, G.M. (born 1987), and a treasury associate, I.P. (born 1982).

Macura is suspected of abusing his position to illegally extract the funds, defrauding Alta Banka of exactly 45,556,596,250 dinars—an amount worth more than $427 million—according to the Interior Ministry and the Public Prosecutor’s Office for Organized Crime.

title: Seven Arrested in International Operation Targeting Investment Fraud
content:
Authorities from seven countries seized more than 100 servers and arrested seven people suspected of being involved in an alleged investment fraud that may have cost victims in at least 50 countries more than $4.6 million. 

Tuesday’s operation, led by German prosecutors and supported by Europol and Eurojust, targeted a company that operated in Cyprus and Israel and supplied platforms to criminal groups running call centers in Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia. 

The scheme relied on misleading online advertisements promising high returns from cryptocurrency, foreign exchange, and stock trading. Victims were encouraged to make larger deposits after their accounts showed fictitious profits, but then withdrawals were subsequently blocked. The investigation began in 2022 after a German couple reported being unable to recover their investments.

title: Indonesia Asks Russia to Stop Recruiting Its Citizens for Ukraine War
content:
Indonesia’s government has asked Russia to cease recruiting its citizens to fight in the war against Ukraine after new data showed a surge of Indonesians joining the conflict.

The growth in mercenary recruits comes amid Indonesian government concerns that citizens of the Southeast Asian country have been tricked into joining the Russian military under the guise of civilian employment.

"The Indonesian government has asked the Russian government to take the necessary steps to ensure that Indonesian citizens are not recruited into the military or other military-related formations in Russia through any means," Indonesian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Yvonne Mewengkang said in a statement reported Sunday by state news agency Antara.

Mewengkang said Indonesia requested to be added to a list of countries whose citizens are exempt from official Russian military recruitment, Antara reported, adding she expected the measure to be implemented “effectively and as soon as possible.”

title: Alleged Turkish Crime Boss Assassinated Inside Spanish Hospital Room
content:
An alleged Turkish crime syndicate leader who survived an assassination attempt some two weeks earlier was fatally shot inside a Spanish hospital room early Thursday in a highly coordinated hit.

Catalonia’s regional police force, the Mossos d'Esquadra, announced they are investigating the fatal shooting of an admitted patient at a hospital in Tarragona. While police placed the case under a judicial secrecy order, a law enforcement source confirmed to OCCRP that the victim was Mekin Büyükdeniz, a member of the Ten Brothers criminal group.

According to Turkish media, the Küçükçekmece Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office formally named Büyükdeniz in prosecutorial filings as the operational leader of the so-called “10 Brothers” gang. In the organizational hierarchy documented in the prosecutor's investigation, the syndicate was identified as a family-centered armed network directed by the Büyükdeniz brothers.

title: Criminal Probe Launched in South Africa Over Contraband Baobabs Bound for Georgia
content:
South African authorities have opened a criminal investigation into the attempted illegal export of five baobab trees to Georgia, halting a massive shipment at the coastal port of Durban after discovering the exporter lacked required environmental permits.

The five trees, estimated to be between 200 and 300 years old and weighing up to 30 tons each, remain impounded at a Durban logistics warehouse while investigators build a case under the country's forestry laws.

Under South Africa’s National Forests Act, the indigenous baobab is a protected species. It is illegal to cut down, harvest, transport, or export live specimens without explicit authorization from environmental regulators. While South Africa permits the commercial trade of processed baobab derivatives—such as fruit powder, seed oil, and cosmetic extracts—under strict licensing, the live specimen trade is tightly restricted to protect the slow-growing trees from international exploitation.

title: Iraqi MP Gets Six Years, $20M Fine for Oil Graft
content:
A specialized anti-corruption court in Iraq sentenced lawmaker Muthanna al-Samarrai to six years in prison and ordered him to repay nearly $20 million for exploiting his position to profit from state oil contracts.

Al-Samarrai, who heads the Sunni political bloc Azm Alliance, used his parliamentary oversight role to benefit from public works and procurement deals involving the state-owned North and South Refineries companies. The lawmaker played a direct role in awarding contracts and steering payments to associates through four private companies, according to Iraq’s Federal Integrity Commission. The court ordered him to return 30 billion Iraqi dinars ($19.81 million) in illicit gains following his arrest in June 2026 alongside a former deputy oil minister.

title: Lawyers for ‘King of the South’ Try to Chip Away at U.S. Drug Trafficking Case
content:
Attorneys for alleged South American drug trafficker Sebastián Marset have asked a federal judge to halt the search of a potentially pivotal cellular phone until the U.S. government explains how it took control of the device from Bolivia.

Marset, a Uruguayan national and self-proclaimed “King of the South,” was arrested in March in a pre-dawn raid in Santa Cruz, Bolivia. Soon after his arrest, he was expelled to Peru and then whisked to the U.S. where he faces money laundering, drug trafficking and narco terrorism charges.

Law enforcement officers in Bolivia seized three phones from the house where they arrested Marset. However, it has emerged that they seized a fourth phone from an adjacent house.

Defense lawyers say in their motion — dated October 23 — that “it is impossible” for them to “be certain as to the timing of the search and whether it was done at the behest of the DEA [Drug Enforcement Administration] or was otherwise valid under Bolivian law.”

They argue that they weren’t notified about the fourth phone, which was a potential key piece of evidence for months, hampering their efforts and raising questions about the integrity of the operation.

title: Flávio Bolsonaro Flees Brazil After Election Defeat and Amid Fraud Probes
content:
Just three days after securing more than 59 million votes in a fiercely contested presidential runoff, Flávio Bolsonaro fled Brazil on Tuesday and landed in the United States, halting investigations at home over his alleged ties to a banker accused of financial fraud.

A senior U.S. State Department official confirmed Tuesday that the U.S. "State Department will issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and his family and allow them entry into the United States."

Argentina's National Directorate of Migration (DNM) confirmed on the social network X that Flávio—son of the convicted former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro—crossed into Argentina through the Tancredo Neves International Bridge, which connects the Brazilian city of Foz do Iguaçu with Argentina’s city of Puerto Iguazú.

Accompanied by his wife and two daughters, Bolsonaro then boarded a private jet that made a short stop in Ecuador before landing in Miami, Florida.

title: China Sentences Ex Anti-Graft Official to Suspended Death for Bribery
content:
A Chinese court sentenced a former senior anti-graft official at the China ​Securities Regulatory Commission, to a suspended death sentence for accepting more than 436 million yuan ($65.4 million) in bribes.

Between 1998 and 2025, Wang Huimin abused his positions in the northwestern Xinjiang region and at the national securities regulator to secure business and fundraising favors for companies and individuals in exchange for the illicit payments, the state-run Xinhua news agency reported.

A suspended death sentence gives the 67-year-old Wang Huimin a two-year reprieve from execution, after which the penalty is automatically commuted to life in prison under Chinese law.

title: Russian Billionaire Takes Tiny Norwegian News Outlet to Court in London
content:
Russian tycoon Vitaly Orlov is suing The Barents Observer, a small Norwegian news outlet, over its reporting on sanctions against his fishing company. 

The Barents Observer is a six-person non-profit newsroom in Kirkenes, a town of about 7,000 people in Norway’s far north. But the lawsuit isn’t taking place there — or even in Norway. Instead, Orlov has lodged a defamation suit in the High Court of London.

“We don’t even have money for plane tickets to go to the court,” said Editor in Chief Thomas Nilsen.

“It’s just not possible for us to defend ourselves against all of the claims,” he told OCCRP’s Norwegian media partner, NRK, adding that if Orlov is awarded some legal costs, The Barents Observer “will go bankrupt.” 

Orlov’s fishing company, Norebo JSC, said in a statement provided to OCCRP that the choice of London as a venue for the lawsuit was related to the fact that The Barents Observer publishes in English.

“The Barents Observer is a Norwegian publication that publishes in English and now complains at being sued in England. This is the very country The Barents Observer has courted,” the company said.
snippet: Russian tycoon Vitaly Orlov is suing The Barents Observer, a small Norwegian news outlet, over its reporting on sanctions against his fishing company.

title: U.S. Court Sentences Lender to 15 Years over $76M Ponzi Scheme
content:
A U.S. federal court has sentenced a businessman to 15 years in prison for his role in running a Ponzi scheme that defrauded hundreds of investors out of millions of dollars. According to a statement from the Department of Justice, Edwin Brant Frost IV, the founder of a conservative, Christian lending firm in Georgia, defrauded more than 300 investors out of over $76 million in a massive Ponzi scheme. Frost, who was convicted of wire fraud in May after pleading guilty, will also have to pay back over $76 million in restitution to victims.

According to federal prosecutors, Frost's now-defunct company, First Liberty Building and Loan, LLC, ran the Ponzi scheme between at least 2021 and July 2025. Frost scammed investors by claiming he was making high-interest, short-term “bridge loans” to small businesses. Prosecutors stated that after most of the bridge loans defaulted, Frost began using new investor funds to pay interest to existing investors, while secretly diverting at least $5 million for lavish personal purchases and political contributions.

title: ‘Students Have Won’: Overwhelming Turnout Shatters Serbia’s Entrenched Regime
content:
When a handful of university students first spilled onto the streets two years ago to protest the deadly collapse of a railway station canopy, Serbia’s state-run media dismissed them as unruly kids merely looking for an excuse to cut class.

They were grieving the 16 people crushed to death and demanding accountability for what they condemned as lethal state corruption and crony contracting, bearing banners that read: “Corruption kills” and “Your hands are bloody.”

But those scattered demonstrations soon swelled into a generational revolt. Over two relentless years, the students slept in occupied lecture halls, barnstormed rural strongholds where state television branded them foreign mercenaries, and punctured a pervasive climate of fear with biting wit and viral banners.

On Sunday, the kids actually did it.

In a stunning ballot-box upset that shattered Aleksandar Vučić’s 14-year grip on power, Serbia’s student-led movement defeated the Balkan country’s formidable ruling machine, clinching a triumph so historic that even its young architects were left reeling in disbelief.

title: FBI Cybercrime Operation Nets Nine Arrests in Nigeria
content:
The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) announced on Monday the arrest of nine people in Nigeria as part of an international operation targeting cybercrime scam centers. According to a statement by FBI Director, Kash Patel, the operation resulted in identifying a total of $11 million in “potentially freezable funds” across multiple countries.

The crackdown, code-named Operation Blackout, saw law enforcement confiscate 53 electronic devices used in the cybercrime operations. Patel added that the operation is aimed at dismantling international cybercriminal networks responsible for "stealing billions from Americans.”

title: Hungarian Tycoon’s Firm Funded Pro-Orbán Advertising Agency, Records Show
content:
A firm owned by Hungarian construction mogul László Szíjj — who amassed a fortune under previous Prime Minister Viktor Orbán — donated about $863,000 to Megafon, a political advertising agency that promoted the former ruling party. 

The donations are detailed in two years of annual financial statements from Szíjj’s firm, Vakond Via Kft., which were examined by OCCRP and Direkt36. The company made “cash grants” that totaled 300 million Hungarian forints to Megafon Digital Incubator Center, adding up to about $252,000 in 2024, and $611,000 the following year.

Launched in 2020, Megafon became one of Hungary’s most influential political advertising agencies, mainly running social media campaigns in support of Orbán’s Fidesz party.

But since Orbán’s stunning electoral defeat in April, after 16-years in power, Megafon has kept a low profile. The company’s website was taken offline in August, and its employees have fallen from 72 to three, according to information from a firm that provides commercial registry data.

Neither Megafon nor Szíjj responded to requests for comment.
